- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in next 7–10 days; apply downward correction of 2–5% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture long-term mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish, add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, model may overfit recent trends; apply smoothing or reduce volatility weight in forecast.
